## "Continue the YM-to-Weil-form investigation in `/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted…": /Users/ebbaker/.codex/attachments/170ac172-7598-4d52-a797-59b9d7f21cc9/Pasted text.txt

## My request:
I’ll read the pasted request and the repository’s investigation notes, then continue from the current state.

The elementary exclusions appear to hold within their stated scope. One distinction needs correction in the outline: an exact pairing automatically induces translations on its source image; requiring a separately identified YM generator is an additional assumption. I’m checking global extension and arithmetic trace mechanisms without making that extra assumption a prerequisite.

I’m using the PDF skill to inspect the decisive theorem statements and formulas in the primary papers. The comparison will separate results that fix the YM state, results that construct an arithmetic representation, and results that could identify the pairing between them.

The arithmetic literature supplies a useful global structure: Meyer derives a character formula containing both the prime and archimedean terms from Poisson summation. It does not supply a positive YM pairing. I’m checking whether transporting that representation into YM would impose stronger conditions than the original problem, including restrictions on repeated zeros.

I have a concrete route to develop: determine the pairing first on separated supports, then prove that the remaining local ambiguity has only three constants. With those constants fixed, the result would identify the full Weil form at every support length without a separately chosen translation generator. The hard missing step is still deriving the separated-support identity from actual YM observables.

The three-constant determination theorem is now written with a proof and a family showing why all three constants are needed. I also found a limitation of the current boundary model: its matrix multiplication algebra has a tracial state, so its modular flow is trivial. A nontrivial modular proposal would require a different algebra or state.

The comparison now favors direct source occurrence plus a mixed arithmetic identity, with compact extension as a supporting tool. I’ve also proved a sharper conditional test: an exact pairing forces a discrete spectrum on its source image. That rules out identifying its translations with vacuum wedge boosts under the stated relativistic hypotheses, while leaving the broader YM existence problem open.
The drafts are saved. I’m checking the new proofs and literature claims once more, particularly the assumptions needed to turn finite source compatibility into one global map.

The final check confirms the main distinction: a separately identified native generator is optional, but genuine YM source content remains essential. The new determination theorem reduces the unresolved matching problem to a precise identity; it does not supply that identity. The earlier notes are unchanged, and the links and file sizes pass the repository checks.
